concept: Sum and evaluate: every implementation of a contract is another way to the same output. world.sum(contract, inputs) runs each (pinned by a fill; own receipt and cache) and records the provenance polynomial, one monomial per way (the implementation and every implementation its trace called); world.evaluate(polynomial, semiring, valuation) maps it into a Capability Lab semiring (boolean, counting, tropical, viterbi, lineage) afterwards, running nothing. The algebra is the Lab's own (src/lab, pinned), not a second copy. Inside an implementation, ctx.sum(contract, args, { slot }) does the same for a child contract (each way a child call; a throwing way recorded, not thrown); the node records its sums and the polynomial expands through them (this node × its calls × Σ over each sum's ways), and its cache entry depends on the set of implementations, valid until one is added or removed.
status: proposed (branch claude/pxc-kernel-sum; Sam merges or not)
source: Sam, 22–23 Oct 2026 (thro / ConstraintLab: each card style is another way; Capability Lab first, a second use sublates into the kernel; ChainSpot as the third use)
forcedBy: first use: Capability Lab src/semiring (semiring.product, provenance.evaluate; Lab grade 277/277); second use: PxCube thro ways.mjs, 'every way this disc could be a card' = Σ over 11 layouts of (layout × keeps your order), evaluated in five semirings (iter-35); pending third: ChainSpot tee pad pose under the 5 s phone budget; ctx.sum: the ChainSpot handoff (a pose implementation summing its detectors)
evidence: test/kernel-sum.test.mjs: evaluate(sum) equals the Lab's provenance.evaluate in all five semirings; evaluation runs nothing; deletion removes exactly the terms using an input; a throwing way is a missing term with its error; a second sum is all cache hits with the same polynomial; run under a fill equals that fill's term, and AMBIGUOUS stays run's; ctx.sum: a way summing two detectors expands into two monomials and evaluates as the factored form (tropical, viterbi, counting); deleting a detector removes only its monomials; a throwing detector is a missing inner term; a second sum is a cache hit with the same polynomial, invalidated by adding a detector (two source mutations each fail these)
hegelWittgenstein: Hegel: the alternatives are not discarded when one is chosen; the fill chooses, the sum keeps every way as a moment of the result (Aufhebung). Wittgenstein: 'the same output' is said in many ways; the semiring is which language game you ask it in (can it, how many, how cheap, how sure, from what).

concept: Timing: every call is timed by the kernel on an injected clock (createWorld({ clock })), in a side record (run(...).timing, world.timing(runId)) that is never in a receipt or trace, never hashed and never read by a decision. Each call records ms, selfMs and a ledger whose remainders are signed and named by where they sit; children that ran together report their overlap, so rows − overlap = ms for every call; any call whose own time is 5% of the run or more is flagged opaque. Implementations are hashed once, at registration (impl.code). world.runAsync and ctx.callAsync run Calculations that wait, with the parent passed explicitly across the await; a call that waited is impure unless its implementation declared pure: true; run keeps ASYNC_RUN.
status: proposed (branch claude/pxc-kernel-sum; Sam merges or not)
source: Sam, 23 Oct 2026 ('PxC is designed to auto instrument every Calculation'; 'that's what spans are for: is this conserved over this span?'); the ChainSpot PxC expert's answer, relay file 02 (Drive, 23 Oct 2026)
forcedBy: first use: PxCube thro, whose tap latency (about 1 s) had no instrument until a hand-written timing.mjs (iter-41..45), whose module-level current call does not cross an await; second use: ChainSpot's provider gateway (an onCall sidecar never hashed, an async gateway clocking across the await, a sha256 of each operation's source on every run) and toolkit profile (the 5% opaque hot spot; a max(0, …) remainder the expert says should be signed)
evidence: test/kernel-timing.test.mjs (12): ms, selfMs and the ledger close exactly on an injected clock; two clocks give byte-identical receipts, traces and cache work; a clock that steps back shows a negative remainder and the books still close; 95% is flagged opaque and 4% is not; no Function.prototype.toString during a run; ctx.callAsync keeps its parent across the await and a later ctx.call lands under it too; parallel waits report their overlap; two runAsync and a sync run get distinct ids; run keeps ASYNC_RUN and ctx.callAsync in a sync run is ASYNC_IN_SYNC_RUN; an async call is impure unless declared pure; the observer sees the timing; a sync implementation gives the same receipt under run and runAsync. The rest of the suite is unchanged (the 3 FRICTION failures are the baseline).
hegelWittgenstein: Hegel: what the measure leaves over is not nothing; named by its boundary, the remainder becomes a moment of the account instead of its excuse. Wittgenstein: a clock in the identity would make 'the same calculation' mean 'the same calculation at the same moment', a different language game; time stays a report about the run, not a fact of what was computed.
